Senior Academics Urge Government Reconsideration on Cancelling Latin Excellence Programme

Academics Appeal to Education Secretary

A group of senior university academics and representatives from classical studies departments and learned societies across the UK have issued a public appeal to the education secretary. They are urging the government to reconsider its decision to terminate funding for the Latin excellence programme, which was recently slated for cancellation.

The signatories, representing institutions including the universities of Oxford, Durham, London, and Cardiff, expressed deep concern over the timing and impact of the decision. They noted that ending the funding mid-year is particularly disheartening for students currently working toward their GCSEs at key stage 4, and they have requested that the scheme be allowed to run at least until the end of the current academic year.

Impact on Non-Selective State Schools

Launched to broaden educational horizons, the Latin excellence programme currently operates in 40 non-selective state schools. Many of these participating institutions are situated in economically deprived areas. According to the academics, more than a third of the programme's 5,000-plus pupils are eligible for free school meals. Proponents argue this high uptake demonstrates the scheme's success in providing equitable access to subjects traditionally less common in state education.

Advocates emphasize that studying Latin offers students cognitive and linguistic benefits, including a deeper understanding of English word roots, exposure to ancient history, archaeology, and art, and the intellectual confidence derived from mastering an ancient language.

Context, Uncertainties, and Verification

The public appeal highlights a growing debate regarding curriculum priorities, equity, and funding allocation in the UK education sector. While supporters maintain the programme aligns with broader educational goals by inspiring and challenging disadvantaged students, the government's official rationale for the termination has not been detailed in the open letter.

Readers seeking to verify the original announcement and read the full correspondence can consult the published letter in The Guardian at the official source link: https://www.theguardian.com/education/2025/jan/12/axing-the-latin-excellence-scheme-a-classic-mistake.
